subtype: Approach: copying a topper's timetable without fit [Pitfall]
passage: Sunday night. It is over. Two weeks ago I copied Damini's timetable from her post: wake at 5, study till midnight, one hour of break in total. She looked so calm in the photo! Week one I was fine, proud even. But school starts at 7:30 and I am useless after ten. By Thursday I was nodding through Chemistry, on Friday I slept through the alarm, and today I lay on the bed and could not open a single book. I was so tired I threw out the whole timetable, even the good parts. Now I have nothing, and nine weeks to boards. Damini's routine works for Damini. Somehow I forgot to ask what works for me. Rajni

qa.q: At what time did the copied timetable have Rajni wake up?
qa.a: The copied timetable had Rajni wake up at 5.

qa.q: What is Rajni feeling as the entry ends?
qa.a: Exhausted, discouraged and a bit regretful about throwing out even the useful parts. 😔
Build a schedule around Rajni's own energy and school hours, giving the hard subjects the hours when concentration is best.

qa.q: How might Damini see Rajni's failed routine?
qa.a: As a sign that a routine made for one person may not suit another, since Damini's plan works for Damini.

grounding: Rajni adopts a 5 am to midnight routine from a social media post without fitting it to Rajni's own energy and school hours, and abandons the whole schedule.
